name: Therapy-related Acute Myeloid Leukemia and Myelodysplastic Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2016)

criteria.description: History of prior exposure to cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiation therapy
Presence of dysplasia in one or more myeloid cell lines in bone marrow
Blast count ≥20% in peripheral blood or bone marrow for AML diagnosis
Presence of characteristic cytogenetic abnormalities associated with therapy-related disease (e.g., deletions of chromosomes 5 or 7)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: History of prior cytotoxic therapy plus morphologic evidence of myelodysplasia or ≥20% blasts in blood or marrow
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of de novo AML/MDS and consideration of latency period after therapy.

pathognomonic.notes: Presence of immature myeloid cells in peripheral blood
searchTerms: immature white blood cells in blood

pathognomonic.notes: Morphologic abnormalities in myeloid lineage cells

common.symptomName: Anemia with pallor and dyspnea on exertion
searchTerms: low red blood cells with pale skin
paleness and shortness of breath on exertion

common.symptomName: Thrombocytopenia leading to easy bruising and petechiae
searchTerms: low platelets causing bruises and spots
easy bruising with small red dots
petechiae and bleeding from low platelets
bleeding under skin due to thrombocytopenia

common.notes: Increased susceptibility to bacterial and fungal infections
searchTerms: immune weakness with low white cells
fatigue due to anemia or low cells

occasional.notes: May reflect inflammatory response or infection
searchTerms: temperature rise with no infection found

occasional.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to extramedullary hematopoiesis

rare.notes: Due to high blast counts causing microvascular occlusion
searchTerms: lung problems from blood cell buildup

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing blasts and dysplastic cells
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT may show infiltrates if leukostasis or infection present
Bone marrow biopsy demonstrating dysplasia and blast infiltration
genetic: Cytogenetic abnormalities including deletions of chromosomes 5q, 7q, or complex karyotype
Mutations in TP53, RUNX1, or other myeloid-associated genes
other: History of prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy
Latency period typically 2-10 years after exposure

distinguishingFeatures: No prior exposure to chemotherapy or radiation

redFlags: Rapidly increasing blast count in peripheral blood
Signs of leukostasis such as respiratory distress or neurological deficits
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Vardiman JW, et al. Therapy-related myeloid neoplasms: WHO classification and clinical features. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2010.
